10-12M. MOS 12M--Firefighter, CMF 12 (Rescind) 202510)
(Army Civilian Acquired Skills Program (ACASP) designated MOS
a. Major duties. The firefighter supervises or provides fire prevention and protection, firefighting, technical
rescue, urban search and rescue and hazardous materials response capabilities to prevent or minimize
injury, loss of life, and property and the environment throughout a range of military operations. Duties for
MOS 12M at each level of skill are:
       (1) MOSC 12M1O. The Firefighter performs Fire and Emergency Services (F&ES) tasks under the
direction of the Lead Firefighter and Station Chief. Their duties include Performing rescue and firefighting
operations during structural fires, aircraft firefighting (ARFF) emergencies, vehicle emergencies and
wildland fires; performing emergency response duties during hazardous materials incidents to include
ordnance; performing urban search and rescue and technical rescue duties. The Fire Truck
Driver/Operator performs as the Driver/Operator of an engineer F&ES vehicle. They maintain firefighting
equipment and vehicles during emergency and non-emergency operations. They must be licensed both
through Army drivers training and the specific driver requirements outlined in DoDM 6055.06 to operate
F&ES vehicles assigned to the team. Driver/Operators must be certified to the level of Driver Operator-
Pumper and Driver Operator-ARFF prior to performing duties in the Driver/Operator positions on the
Tactical Firefighting Truck (TFFT). To perform duties as the Driver/Operator for the Heavy Expanded
Mobility Tactical Truck Based Water Tender (HEWATT), the Driver/Operator must be certified to the
Mobile Water Supply (MWS) Apparatus level. Both Fire Apparatuses require the Driver/Operator to be
Heavy Expanded Mobility Tactical Truck (HEMTT) driver qualified.
       (2) MOSC 12M2O. The Lead Firefighter leads team personnel at the scene of an emergency and
conducts and records team level training as directed by the Station Chief. Their duties include Directing
rescue and firefighting operations during structural fires, ARFF emergencies, vehicle emergencies, and
wildland fires; directing emergency response crews during hazardous materials incidents to include
ordnance; and directing urban search and rescue and technical rescue operations as directed by the Fire
Chief or Fire Marshal.
       (3) MOSC 12M3O. The Station Chief/Fire Team Chief duties include Supervising the team in all
F&ES missions. Acting as Senior Fire Officer during initial response to an emergency. In the absence of a
supporting headquarters, they assume responsibilities of Fire Chief. The Fire Inspector provides fire
inspection and prevention capability in support of activities in a base camp. The fire inspector provides
expeditionary fire inspections and limited fire prevention functions including hazard assessments, public
fire safety education and facilities plans reviews. Additional duties include maintaining the status of the
F&ES team equipment and supplies for 24-hour continuous missions and resupply after each mission.
Duties may also include coordinating for recharging and servicing of SCBA and firefighting agents for
mission vehicles. In addition, provide resupply for fire extinguishers that are unserviceable for live areas
and structures via contract with local vendors.
       (4) MOSC 12M4O. The Fire Chief is both the Noncommissioned Officer in charge (NCOIC) and
Senior Fire Officer (SFO) for all F&ES at the Army, Corps, Division, and Brigade level for an area of
operations (AO). Their duties consist of: Advising the Fire Marshal, Fire Inspector, mayor cell, forward
engineer support team, and commander of force protection issues relating to F&ES; establishing and
direct F&ES planning and coordination, working with the fire marshal in establishing and directing a Fire
Alarm Communications Center (FACC); providing F&ES management oversight, establishing a fire
prevention and inspection program to include training; providing senior leadership advice on vital
information for minimizing loss of life, property damage, life safety, and limiting damage from fire that
would seriously degrade mission capability. The Fire Chief is designated as incident commander during
F&ES incidents and is the operations section chief or branch director (fire protection) when not employed
as the incident commander in the National Incident Management System (NIMS) hierarchy of incident
command.
b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for award and retention of MOS. Firefighters must possess
the following qualifications unless a waiver is granted by United States Army Engineer School (USAES):
         (1) A physical demands rating of heavy (Black).
         (2) A physical profile of 111121.
         (3) Normal color vision.
         (4) Qualifying scores.
             (a) A minimum score of 88 in aptitude area GM.
              (b) A minimum Occupational Physical Assessment Test (OPAT) score of Standing Long Jump
(LJ) – 0160 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) – 0450 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0160 lbs. and Interval
Aerobic Run (IR) – 0043 shuttles in Physical Demand Category “Heavy” (Black).
          (5) Pass medical screening meeting standards of National Fire Protection Association (NFPA)
standard 1582.
         (6) No record of pyro-phobia, acrophobia, or claustrophobia.
         (7) Must possess a valid motor vehicle license from any of the 50 states or US territories either in
photo ID or paper form in accordance with applicants issuing State or US Territory law(s) or regulations in
order to ship from entry station to BCT or AIT.
         (8) Far visual acuity no worse than 20/100 bilateral, corrected to 20/20
         (9) For initial award of MOS, attend mandatory formal training at Goodfellow AFB, TX, or must
meet the ACASP criteria per Chapter 9-5b (5b) of this pamphlet and paragraph below.
         (10) Firefighter I, Firefighter II, Airport Firefighter, Hazardous Materials Awareness, Hazardous
Materials (HAMZAT) Operations, HAZMAT Ops – Personal Protective Equipment, HAZMAT Ops –
Product Control and Emergency Medical Responder or equivalent in accordance with DoD 6055.06-M.
             (a) In Accordance With (IAW) table 9-1 of this pamphlet, Initial Entry Trainee (IET) who qualifies
under the ACASP will not be required to attend Advanced Individual Training (AIT) for any additional
training. Upon completion of Basic Combat Training (BCT) Soldier Member will be processed IAW initial
assignment instruction.
         (11) MOSC qualification per AR 420-1 at each level of skill.
              (a) All Firefighters must—
                  (1) Maintain current basic life support cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and Automated
External Defibrillator qualifications according to American Red Cross or American Heart Association
standards.
                  (2) Maintain current Emergency Medical Responder certification or obtain a higher
equivalence i.e., EMT/Paramedic.
                  (3) Be awarded and retain MOS 12M
              (b) A Driver/Operator must–
                  (1) Be in the rank of SPC or below.
                  (2) Complete and obtain the F&ES approved Driver/Operator-Pumper, ARFF, and MWS
certifications.
                  (3) Be awarded the duty position of Driver/Operation qualifications are met and reflect in
the DoD Fire Emergency Services Certification Program (FESCP).
              (c) A Lead Firefighter must–
                  (1) Be in the rank of SGT, previously qualified and work as a firefighter and have a
minimum of 1-year on-the-job experience at the position immediately below the target position.
                  (2) Complete Fire Instructor I, Fire Inspector I, Fire Officer I, and Fire Department Incident
Safety Officer within one year of pinning (active duty), two years of pinning (National Guard and
Reserves) to be considered for retention.
                  (3) Be awarded the rating of Lead Firefighter once qualifications are met and reflect in the
DoD FESCP.
              (d) A Station Chief must–
                  (1) Be in the rank of SGT promotable (P) or SSG and previously qualified as a Lead
Firefighter.
                  (2) Complete the Advanced Leaders Course (ALC) for MOS 12M within one year of pinning
(active duty), two years of pinning (National Guard and Reserves) to be considered for retention.
                  (3) Be awarded the rating of Station Chief upon obtaining ALC DA form1059.
              (e) A Fire Chief must–
                  (1) Be in the rank of SSG (P), SFC and previously qualified as a Station Chief.
                  (2) Complete the Senior Leader's Course (SLC) for MOS 12M within one year of pinning
(active duty), two years of pinning (National Guard and Reserves) to be considered for retention.
                  (3) Be awarded the rating of Fire Chief upon obtaining SLC DA 1059.
        (12) Approval and validation to qualify IET for ACASP is through the USAES, Engineer Personnel
Development Office (EPDO).
         (13) All DoD firefighters shall be certified at the next higher level before being eligible for that level
and have a minimum of 1-year on-the-job experience at the position immediately below the target
position, in accordance with DoD 6055.06-M.
        (14) The options available to Army firefighters, in Active, Reserve and National Guard
Components, for fulfilling certification requirements are: attend courses at the Louis F. Garland Fire
Academy, Goodfellow Air Force Base (GAFB), TX (Note: Not all certifications are offered at GAFB); enroll
in USAF Career Development Courses (CDCs) online; or attend International Fire Service Accreditation
Congress (IFSAC) or pro-board accredited courses available through third part firefighting universities
and colleges.
             (a) Soldiers who have completed IFSAC and pro-board accredited training at non-DoD entities
must file for reciprocity through the DoD Fire and Emergency Services Certification Program (FESCP) in
accordance with DoD 6055.06-M. Certification levels of all DoD fire and emergency services personnel, to
include MOS 12M Soldiers, can be viewed and verified on the DoD FESCP website.
        (15) Based on unit mission posture Firefighters at all skill levels may also be required to complete
Rescue Technician I, Technical Rescuer I-Confined Space Rescue I and II, Confined Space Rescue I and
II, Rope Rescue I and II, Structural Collapse Rescue I and II, Trench Rescue I and II, and Vehicle and
Machinery Rescue I and II.
        (16) Firefighters in all ranks are highly encouraged to enroll in and complete the following Federal
Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) certification: IS 100.b Introduction to Incident Command
System, IS 200.b Incident Command System for Single Resources and Initial Actions Incidents, IS 700.a.
An Introduction to NIMS, IS 800.a An Introduction to the National Response Framework.
        (17) In accordance with DoD 6055.06-M, must pass pre-employment medical and physical criteria
contained in NFPA 1582 and NFPA 1580 when published prior to attending formal training. NFPA 1582 is
going away along with NFPA 1583 and will be combined in NFPA 1580.
           c. Additional skill identifiers (ASI). (Note: Refer to table 12-8 Listing of universal ASIs associated
with all enlisted MOS).
              (1) B9—Bradley Fighting Vehicle (BFV) (personnel only).
              (2) P6--Project Management (Skill level 2 thru 6 for personnel only).
              (3) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (skill level 4 through 6 for personnel only) (Effective
202410).
              (4) R7--Army Reconnaissance (Skill level 3-7 personnel only).
           d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to
each skill level are listed in the following tables.
              (1) Table 10-12M-1. Physical requirements.
              (2) Table 10-12M-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (3) Table 10-12M-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
